canonical_name: Girl Up Global Teen Advisor Board
aliases: Girl Up Board of Teen Advisors
organizer: Girl Up (a Global Fund for Children initiative; historically a United Nations Foundation campaign)
organizer_domain_provenance: girlup.org is the organisation's own first-party domain; the programme page, the application-guidance article, the clubs pages and the contact addresses (AWARDS@GIRLUP.ORG, Community@GirlUp.org) are all on it, and the club registration platform runs on the clubs.girlup.org / community.girlup.org subdomains. The application page names Global Fund for Children as co-issuer of the completion certificate, which corroborates the organisational relationship. NOTE: girlup.org returns HTTP 403 to plain server-side fetchers — I could only read it through a real browser session. Any ingestion crawler will need a browser-grade fetch for this domain, not just an allowlist entry. It is a .org and will fail looksOfficial().
eligible_countries: Global — 'Girl Up welcomes citizens from every country to apply.' The 2023-2024 board drew from 14 countries including Türkiye, India, Ghana, Kenya, Canada, UK, Chile, Brazil, Colombia, Peru, UAE, Australia, Bangladesh and the US.

age_range.quote: Must be between the ages of 13-19 at the start of their tenure
age_range.note: See research_notes — an earlier cycle's guidance stated 13-17 plus a high-school-enrolment requirement. Both cannot be current.

prerequisites: Must identify as a girl, woman, or gender expansive youth
Must be fluent and comfortable speaking English

Must have participated in Girl Up programming in the past (a club, a local initiative, a WiSci camp or leadership summit, or the online community) — prior involvement is mandatory, confirmed in the FAQ: 'Yes, you need to have some level of prior involvement with Girl Up to apply.'
duration: One-year term. Minimum commitment of 10 hours per month, including two virtual meetings monthly (typically the second Sunday, 10:00-12:00 EST) plus peer reflection meetings, totalling roughly 3 hours of synchronous meetings a month.
financial_aid: Not a cost — advisors receive an honorarium of $750 USD
selection_process: Written application: five short-answer questions (~50 words each), three essays (~250 words each), and a one-minute video (or a 100-word essay alternative). 'Every year we receive hundreds of applications from leaders around the world. This year we plan to select 10-12 young leaders, making the Global Teen Advisory Board highly competitive.' Evaluated on commitment to global gender justice, leadership potential, proven community impact, ability to innovate, and commitment to diversity, equity and inclusion. No deadline extensions are offered.
award_or_output: One-year appointed advisory role; $750 USD honorarium; certificate and/or letter of recognition from Girl Up and Global Fund for Children; direct mentorship from a Girl Up staff member; opportunity to speak at Girl Up / Global Fund for Children events.
leadership_evidence: VERY STRONG, and rare for this age band because the responsibility is contractual rather than ceremonial. The official application page states advisors 'Serve on technical committees to work directly with Girl Up staff on programmatic, strategic, and operational deliverables' and 'Serve as a representative for Girl Up in public spaces', advise on partners and programmes, and collaborate with regional staff on events and campaigns — with a floor of 10 hours a month for a year and a $750 honorarium attached. The selection ratio is published as 10-12 chosen from hundreds of global applicants. A selected teenager can demonstrate: appointed to the governing advisory board of an international NGO; delivered on named operational committees; represented the organisation publicly. This is the shape ORYN's catalogue was missing entirely.

research_notes: CYCLE STATE — READ CAREFULLY. Today is 2026-08-21. The application page states 'The 2026-2027 Global Teen Advisor Board will serve a one-year term from September 2026 – August 2027' with 'APPLY BY August 1' and an explicit no-extensions FAQ. The 1 August 2026 deadline has therefore PASSED by 20 days; the incoming cohort's term has not yet begun. I have marked this VERIFIED_HISTORICAL rather than VERIFIED_CURRENT for that reason: every fact is verified and current, but the application window is shut. The next opening date is not published. 'Applications closed' does not mean discontinued — this is an annual programme and the site is actively maintained (a related article is dated 11 July 2026). PAGE INCONSISTENCY FLAGGED, NOT SILENTLY RESOLVED: the programme overview page at /programs/teen-advisors still advertises 'Applications for the 2025-2026 Global Teen Advisor Board are now open! APPLY BY JANUARY 26' and shows a 2023-2024 board snapshot, while the linked application article's body describes the 2026-2027 board with an August 1 deadline. The two Girl Up pages disagree with each other. I have taken the article body as authoritative because it is internally consistent and names explicit term dates, but the overview page is stale and a counselor should not quote its January date. AGE CONFLICT FLAGGED: the current article says 13-19 at start of tenure with no schooling requirement; a prior cycle's guidance (surfaced in search, not fetched by me) said 13-17 and required enrolment in secondary school until at least May 2026. These are different cycles' rules. I recorded 13-19 because that is what the page I actually read says, and I am flagging that a 18-19 year old reading a stale third-party listing might wrongly self-exclude, or a 13-year-old might wrongly self-include, depending on which they find. TÜRKIYE RELEVANCE: the 2023-2024 board explicitly included a Turkish advisor, which is direct evidence that Turkish applicants are selectable — unusually concrete for ORYN's home market.

canonical_name: Girl Up Club (found and lead a chapter)
organizer: Girl Up (a Global Fund for Children initiative)
organizer_domain_provenance: Same as the Girl Up Teen Advisor record: girlup.org is first-party, with club registration served from clubs.girlup.org and community.girlup.org and support at Community@GirlUp.org. Same 403-to-server-fetchers caveat; a browser-grade fetch is required.
eligible_countries: Global — the network spans 155 countries and all 50 U.S. states
grade_range: Middle school, junior high, high school, homeschooled, or college — separate registration paths exist for school Club Leaders and university Campus Leaders
prerequisites: Gather a team — a club, not a solo activity
Register the club with Girl Up
selection_process: Registration, not competitive selection. Registering unlocks Girl Up's tools, resources and opportunities.
award_or_output: A registered chapter within a network of 7,850+ clubs; access to Girl Up's structured programming in organising, advocacy, fundraising and communications; the Club and role become a named credential used in Girl Up's own Teen Advisor application ('If you have participated in a Girl Up Club, don't forget to include the Club name and your title, and describe your responsibilities').
leadership_evidence: GENUINE FOUNDER/LEADER ROLE — this is the entry rung, and its value is structural rather than selective. There is no competitive gate: any student can register a club. What makes it real is that the student must recruit and run a team, and that Girl Up itself treats the Club title and responsibilities as evidence (its Teen Advisor application asks applicants to name the club, their title, their responsibilities, and to quantify achievements — educational sessions, film screenings, fundraisers, awareness campaigns, service projects, meetings with local decision-makers). A student can demonstrate: founded and led a registered chapter of an international organisation with N members; ran N events; raised $N. HONEST CAVEAT: because registration is open to anyone, the credential carries no selectivity signal at all — its worth is entirely in what the student actually does with it. A counselor should treat this as a vehicle for building leadership evidence, not as an achievement in itself, and should be explicit with the student about that distinction. Notably, prior Girl Up involvement is a hard prerequisite for the Teen Advisor board, so founding a club is the standard on-ramp to the far more selective advisory role.

age_range.quote: You are under 20 years of age
age_range.note: No minimum age is stated on the official criteria page. I did not invent one.

prerequisites: Residency: 'You can only apply to AYC in the country that you are a resident of'
An existing original idea the candidate developed themselves from empathy with a problem
An existing team the candidate built around that idea
Demonstrated improvement to people's lives or the environment
Willingness to co-lead the global Everyone a Changemaker movement
financial_aid: 'Reimbursements are available for all candidates to cover panel related expenses like domestic travel, accommodation, and food. Candidates can also bring a parent or adult ally during the visit.'
selection_process: Four stages. Stage 1: online nomination (self or third-party) and screening. Stage 2: national review with the Ashoka team in the candidate's country. Stage 3: international review with an Ashoka Senior Leader and young changemakers from the global network. Stage 4: in-person selection panel including senior social entrepreneurs, journalists and other leaders. A nomination is an expression of interest for the next selection panel in that country; a nomination is not required in order to apply.
individual_or_team: individual founder, assessed on the team they built
award_or_output: Induction into the global Ashoka Young Changemakers network; co-leadership opportunities within the Everyone a Changemaker movement; peer network, mentorship and platforms
latest_verified_cycle: Open year-round as of 2026-08-21, in six countries only
leadership_evidence: VERY STRONG AND EXPLICITLY DEFINED — Ashoka publishes its leadership criterion verbatim, which is unusually useful for a counselor. To qualify the candidate must satisfy three tests: 'Your idea — You deeply empathized with a problem and from that understanding developed your own original idea for addressing it'; 'Your team — You built a team around this idea. You lead by helping others lead, helping them realise they can create positive change'; 'Your world changed — You helped improve people's lives and the environment around them.' Selection therefore certifies founding, team-building and demonstrated impact, adjudicated across a national review, an international review and an in-person panel of senior social entrepreneurs. A selected young person can demonstrate an externally-panelled verdict that they founded and led a real initiative with real outcomes. MAJOR LIMITATION FOR ORYN, stated plainly: this is unreachable for ORYN's home market. Residency in Nigeria, Brazil, India, Bangladesh, Indonesia or the US is mandatory. No Turkish, European, UK or Middle Eastern student can apply. The official page directs others to 'write to your Ashoka country office for youth-related opportunities in your country' — a lead worth chasing for Türkiye, but not a verified opportunity today.

organizer_domain_provenance: STRONG — this is the cleanest provenance in the batch. GOV.UK's official business-finance-support directory, published by the Department for Business and Trade, lists Young Enterprise as a business support programme and links directly to https://www.young-enterprise.org.uk/ as its site. A .gov.uk government page naming and linking the .org.uk domain is exactly the corroboration an ingestion pipeline needs to add young-enterprise.org.uk to officialDomains. The .org.uk domain itself would otherwise fail looksOfficial().
prerequisites: Must go through a participating school or college — there is no individual entry route
program_dates: Schools can launch the programme any time from September to March
duration: Flexible — from 12 weeks up to one academic year

cost.payer: the school or college, not the individual student

selection_process: No competitive selection to enter — schools and colleges enrol. Competition comes afterwards: 'Student companies can participate in competitions at a local, county and regional level to win a place at our Company of the Year national final.'
award_or_output: A real trading student company with a business bank account (via Card One Money), products or services sold at events and through the YE Trading Station, and managed finances; progression through local, county and regional competitions to the Company of the Year national final.
latest_verified_cycle: Running — September to March launch window
leadership_evidence: STRONG AND SPECIFIC — the official page states 'students make all major decisions about their student company, from sourcing start up capital to choosing director roles, launching a product or service and managing their company finances.' The company opens a real business bank account and trades with the public. A student can therefore demonstrate a named directorship (Managing Director, Finance Director and so on) in a company that raised its own capital, sold real products to real customers, and reported real financials — with revenue figures a counselor can actually ask about. Progression to a regional or national Company of the Year final adds a selectivity signal on top. This is one of the very few opportunities at this age that produces genuine, auditable entrepreneurship evidence rather than a pitch-deck exercise.

NOT YET DONE: I did not fetch an EU-institutional or government page linking jaeurope.org. It is a .org and will fail looksOfficial().
prerequisites: Delivered through participating schools with teacher facilitation — no individual entry route is described
selection_process: No selection to enter; students compete afterwards in 'company of the year' competitions against other schools.
award_or_output: A real mini-company: elected board of directors, share capital raised, bank account opened, market research, business plan, product or service developed and traded with the public, finances managed, trade fairs attended, and entry into company-of-the-year competitions. Over 360,000 students enrol annually, creating 30,000 mini-companies.
leadership_evidence: STRONG, and the elected-board mechanic is the key detail. The official page states students 'elect a board of directors from amongst their peers, raise share capital, and market and finance a product or service.' A student can therefore demonstrate an elected office — chosen by peers, not self-declared — in an entity that raised capital and traded publicly. This directly answers the failure mode ORYN's own spec calls out (Phase 6.3: a student should not get a high leadership score merely for typing 'President'): here the title is peer-elected and attached to auditable financial and trading activity. At 30,000 mini-companies a year the programme is common rather than selective, so the differentiator is the company's actual results and the student's specific office, not participation.

The Programme Guide served there is the legally operative document for the programme. As with Euroscola, this is unambiguously official but will FAIL looksOfficial(), which accepts only .edu/.ac./.gov — a pure gate artefact. europa.eu and its subdomains should be added to officialDomains outright.

selection_process: Not an individual competitive selection. A youth organisation, public body, social enterprise or an informal group of young people applies to its National Agency for a grant; participants are then recruited by the applicant organisation or group.
award_or_output: A funded multi-country youth exchange of 5-21 days; for those who apply as an informal group, an EU-funded project they themselves designed and ran
latest_verified_cycle: Programme running; deadlines are set annually per National Agency call, not centrally on the pages fetched
leadership_evidence: POTENTIALLY VERY STRONG — but only on one of the two routes, and the distinction matters enormously for a counselor. Route A, joining an exchange as a participant: this is intercultural exposure, not leadership; the student turns up to a project someone else designed. Route B, applying as an informal group: the Programme Guide states an applicant may be 'An informal group of young people' defined as at least four members aged 13-30 with one representative aged 18 or over. On that route a 16-year-old can co-author and run an EU-funded international project — securing public funding, coordinating partner organisations in other countries, and delivering a 5-21 day programme. That is a genuine, externally-audited project-ownership artefact, and it is one of the very few routes at this age to a real grant from a government body. The 18+ representative requirement means a 16-year-old cannot be the sole formal lead, which should be stated honestly rather than glossed. Note also that group leader roles within an exchange require age 18+, so under-18s cannot hold that specific title.

research_notes: VERIFIED on the European Commission's own Programme Guide and opportunities pages, fetched directly. This is the highest-leverage record in the batch for ORYN's geography: Türkiye is a full participating country, the age floor is 13, and it is fully funded — an unusual combination. DELIBERATE NULLS: deadline and application_open_date. Erasmus+ call deadlines are set annually and administered per National Agency; neither page I fetched published a 2026 or 2027 date, and inventing one would be exactly the error this lane guards against. A follow-up should fetch the Türkiye Ulusal Ajansı call calendar for the current round — that is the single most useful next step for a Turkish student. NOT VERIFIED: the full list of associated third countries (the Programme Guide section I read references the category without enumerating it in that section; Türkiye's eligibility is confirmed via the funding table, which is sufficient for ORYN's purposes but does not let me publish the whole list). PRACTICAL CAVEAT: this is not something a student signs up for on a website. It requires either finding a sending organisation that is running an exchange, or forming a group of four and working with an 18+ representative to apply to a National Agency — a materially higher-effort path than any other record in this batch, which ORYN's effort scoring should reflect.
